walkthroughs.body_html:
Chemistry of the Environment — a core area of GCSE Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Chemistry of the Environment brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Chemistry of the Environment.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: The approximate percentage of nitrogen in clean dry air is:
Which gas is a major cause of acid rain?
options: Sulfur dioxide
Nitrogen
Argon
Oxygen

mcqs.q: Chlorine is added to drinking water in order to:
options: Kill microbes
Remove solid particles
Improve the taste
Add useful minerals

mcqs.q: Which of these is a greenhouse gas?
options: Methane
Nitrogen
Oxygen
Argon

mcqs.q: Is carbon dioxide the main cause of acid rain?
options: Air is mostly carbon dioxide.
No — acid rain is mainly caused by sulfur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen; CO₂ only makes rain very slightly acidic.
Acid rain is caused by oxygen dissolving in rainwater.
Acid rain is caused by carbon dioxide because it forms carbonic acid in water.

mcqs.q: Are global warming and the ozone hole the same problem?
options: Air is mostly carbon dioxide.
Greenhouse gases cool the planet by blocking sunlight.
No — warming is caused by greenhouse gases trapping infrared radiation; ozone depletion is a separate problem with different causes.
Global warming happens because the hole in the ozone layer lets extra heat in.
No — about 78% of dry air is nitrogen; oxygen makes up only about 21%.
Air is mostly carbon dioxide.
Greenhouse gases cool the planet by blocking sunlight.
Air is mostly oxygen because oxygen is the gas we breathe and use.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Water treatment”?
options: Clean dry air is approximately 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen, with small amounts of argon, carbon dioxide and other gases.
Domestic water is treated by sedimentation and filtration to remove solids, then chlorination to kill microbes.
Carbon monoxide, sulfur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen from burning fuels are toxic or cause acid rain and respiratory problems.
Carbon dioxide and methane absorb infrared radiation emitted from the Earth's surface, trapping heat and contributing to climate change.

options: Carbon monoxide, sulfur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen from burning fuels are toxic or cause acid rain and respiratory problems.
Domestic water is treated by sedimentation and filtration to remove solids, then chlorination to kill microbes.
Carbon dioxide and methane absorb infrared radiation emitted from the Earth's surface, trapping heat and contributing to climate change.
